item.title: Tyson Cuts Profit Outlook Again as Beef Segment Worsens
item.description: Tyson Foods Inc. cut its outlook for the fiscal year again as it sees more pressure from its beef segment.

item.title: Saudi Arabia’s Humain Unveils AI Model Based on China’s MiniMax
item.description: Saudi Arabia’s artificial intelligence company Humain has built a national AI platform based on an open model from Chinese lab MiniMax Group Inc., joining a growing list of countries seeking tighter control of the increasingly important technology.

item.title: HTC Brings $499 Vive Eagle Smart Glasses to US Amid Broader Privacy Concerns
item.description: HTC Corp. is rolling out its Vive Eagle smart glasses in the US, entering a market where category leader Meta Platforms Inc. is already facing mounting concerns from consumers over clandestine camera recording.

item.title: Russia’s Oil Revenue Sinks to Six-Month Low as Urals Price Drops
item.description: Russia’s oil revenue slumped to a six-month low in August, reflecting lower export prices and compounding pressure on the Kremlin’s ability to finance its war in Ukraine.

item.title: India RBI Faces About $11 Billion Bill on Foreign Deposits Plan
item.description: India tapped its vast diaspora for a record $127 billion through a special deposit program, a fundraising bonanza that economists say could come with a hefty $10.6 billion bill for the country’s central bank.

item.title: US Stock Futures Rise as Traders Parse Fedspeak, Earnings
item.description: US stock futures posted modest gains Thursday as bond yields stabilized near multi-year highs and investors digested latest commentary from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller. Chip stocks fell after Broadcom Inc.’s results.

item.title: Saudi Firm Humain Eyes $2.5 Billion Fund to Build Data Centers
item.description: Artificial intelligence firm Humain is planning to raise an initial $2.5 billion from global and domestic investors for a fund to invest in data centers in Saudi Arabia, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Campbell’s Shares Slump on Sales Slide, Dividend Cut, Outlook
item.description: Campbell’s Co. shares slumped after the packaged food and snack maker said sales shrank for a fourth straight quarter, cut its dividend and unveiled a cost-savings plan.

item.title: US Trade Gap Widens to Largest Since Early 2025 on AI Push
item.description: The US trade deficit widened sharply in July to the largest since early 2025, reflecting a surge in imports of computers and other technology equipment.

item.title: US Share of Canada’s Exports Drops to 66%, Lowest Outside Pandemic
item.description: Canada’s trade surplus narrowed sharply in July, driven by lower exports of gold and energy, particularly to the US.

item.title: Fed’s Waller Says September Rate Decision Hinges on August CPI
item.description: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said his next decision on interest rates will be “heavily influenced” by August inflation data due next week, adding it may not take much to nudge him toward supporting a rate hike at the Fed’s upcoming policy meeting.

item.title: Investors Predict More Pain for Brazil Insurer After 90% Wipeout
item.description: Investors see few reasons to be optimistic about Hapvida, the Brazilian health insurer and hospital operator plagued by rising costs, constant litigation and an escalating debt load.

item.title: Blackstone’s BCRED Caps Redemptions Again After 10% Seek to Exit
item.description: Blackstone Inc. again limited redemptions from its flagship private credit fund after investors sought to pull 10% of shares, providing an early glimpse at the lasting quarterly withdrawal pressure ahead for the $1.8 trillion market.

item.title: Nvidia Acquires AI Platform Hugging Face for About $13 Billion
item.description: Nvidia Corp. has agreed to acquire artificial intelligence startup Hugging Face in a transaction valued at about $13 billion.

item.title: US Stock Futures Today: Broadcom, HPE, Snowflake, Ultragenyx
item.description: S&P 500 Index futures are little changed as of 7:53 a.m. in New York. Technology shares are in focus, following results from with chipmaker Broadcom and Hewlett Packard Enterprise.

item.title: Rising Yields Seen Pushing Companies to Sell Bonds Sooner
item.description: Wall Street dealers were already bracing for a potential record in September for high-grade US corporate bond sales, and recent surging yields may give the blue-chip companies even more reason to borrow now before funding costs rise further.

item.title: Polish Rates Seen on Hold for Rest of 2026, MPC Member Duda Says
item.description: Poland’s interest rates are set to stay unchanged for the rest of this year, or potentially longer, as inflation may temporarily top the central bank’s tolerance range, according to policymaker Iwona Duda.

item.title: TikTok, YouTube Find Silence Speaks Loudly in Face of Pressure on Child Safety
item.description: The companies are under scrutiny for failing to join rivals on protections for young people

item.title: Bezos’ Blue Origin Has Poached Dozens of Amazon Satellite Engineers
item.description: Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin is developing its planned satellite network with the help of employees poached from another Bezos project: Amazon.com Inc.

item.title: China and Brazil and US Race for Rare Earths
item.description: Beijing controls much of the world’s minerals and mines and perhaps the most important part: the processing.

item.title: Even Rich Brits Are Shopping Second-Hand and Trading Down
item.description: Frugality has become part of the UK’s national mood.

item.title: AstraZeneca, Sanofi, Boehringer Back Owkin AI to Cut Drug Bottlenecks
item.description: AI can produce thousands of drug ideas in seconds. That’s the problem

item.title: US Jobs Report Could Offer Clues on Workforce Participation Drop
item.description: A recent plunge in US labor force participation has sparked competing theories about whether persistent drivers — like aging and immigration — or more temporary seasonal shifts are to blame. Any evidence in upcoming jobs reports could reshape how policymakers view the labor market.

item.title: Wiz Founder Backs Israeli Startup Guardio at $1.1 Billion Value
item.description: Israeli cybersecurity startup Guardio raised funds from investors including Assaf Rappaport, the founder of cloud security firm Wiz, in a round that values the company at $1.1 billion.

item.title: BOJ Data Suggest No Intervention While Officials Vow to Fight On
item.description: Bank of Japan accounts showed no sign of a major intervention in the currency market by Tokyo on Wednesday, suggesting that sharp moves in the exchange rate that day were likely driven by twitchy traders amid a re-calibration of rate hike expectations.

item.title: Global Bond Retreat Slows as Decade-High Yields Tempt Investors
item.description: Global bonds clawed back ground as yields near multi-decade highs proved hard for some investors to resist, even as energy prices keep markets on edge.

item.title: Hungary Central Bank Files Police Report on Overpriced Property
item.description: The National Bank of Hungary pressed charges over fresh instances of suspected embezzlement under its previous governor, related to a series of allegedly overpriced property acquisitions.

item.title: Why Bond Yields Surging Around the World (UST)
item.description: Darrell Duffie thinks the Treasury market is far from fixed.

item.title: Schroders Buys Long-Dated Treasuries Citing Attractive Yields
item.description: British asset manager Schroders Plc has bought more of longer-dated US Treasuries, saying yields have nearly peaked after the recent selloff.
